reasons: The cited paragraphs confirm the gap: Section 11.1 imposes a five-year initial term with auto-renewal and Section 11.2 limits termination to uncured material breach or insolvency, so the absence of any Corio (customer-side) convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a genuine 'missing behaviour' deviation under T4C.

The proposed new Section 11.4 reaches the preferred position exactly: 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, no early-termination fee, and an express bar on Commerce One terminating for convenience during the initial or renewal terms.
Edit is minimal and additive — existing 11.3 text is untouched and a new subsection is inserted at the logically correct place in the termination article; no other clause is disturbed.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact: the clause reads 'Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice', which satisfies the rule in substance even though the interposed 'in whole or in part' defeats the pattern match.

Comment is accurate, correctly identifies our party as Corio, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the 60-day fallback while holding the line on fees and vendor convenience rights; tone and prefix conform.
